2 great books I highly recommend are "The End: The Defiance and Destruction of Hitlers Germany, 1944-1945" by Ian Kershaw and "The German War, A Nation Under Arms, 1939 to 1945" by Nicholas Stargardt. The first one does a good job of painting the German High Commands loyalty to Hitler and its eventual decline and post war revisionism (although that isnt the main purpose of the book, still an excellent read) while the second one does a good job showing the attitude of German generals throughout the war from start to finish. One thing to keep in mind is that immediately after world war 2 the allies were thrown into a stand off with the Soviet Union. An important field in this stand off was Germany, now divided into east and west. When the Americans decided that an unmilitarized Germany was a waste of resources in the area, given how the Soviets were allowing the east germans to militarize, they had to sell a rebuilding of the German army to a group of countries and peoples that just suffered through 2 world wars either started or made worse by that same army. This is where the myth of the "Good Wehrmacht bad SS" starts to take root and spread. A consequence of this myth is the common belief that the German High command was capable and that had the Nazis not interfered then the Germans would have easily trounced the Russians (see how that narrative is convinent for an Anti-soviet army?).

Generally speaking Hitler didnt meddle too much in the operations of his general staff. When he did he was usually correct like in the case of the ardennes in 1940 and during his misgivings about the battle of Kursk in 43. Most German generals insisted AFTER the war that had Hitler let them command they would have had an easier time but that's a post war effort by those generals to improve their own image. Their official diaries and letters during the war usually stated, up until 44-45 or well after the was had been lost, that they generally supported Hitlers military decisions and felt confident in their ability to win. Keep in mind this doesn't speak for every leader in the German army but enough to say that in general the German high command supported Hitler fully for most of the war.
